findings.title: Remove exhausted credentials from the storage that owns them
findings.body: The new lookup can return a credential owned by an external user-storage provider, but the exhaustion branch still calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only removes locally stored credentials. An exhausted external credential therefore remains configured. If the user abandons the subsequent recovery-code setup, the next login can select that empty credential, and RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(), causing an error instead of displaying a usable authentication challenge. Handle external credential exhaustion through the owning provider rather than the local credential-removal API.

findings.title: Exercise single-use consumption in the federated recovery-code test
findings.body: The new test provider accepts any matching recovery code without removing or marking it used, and getCredentials reconstructs a fresh credential from the unchanged list on every call. Consequently, the same recovery code can authenticate indefinitely, the displayed code number never advances, and the exhaustion/reconfiguration path is never exercised. The added integration test checks only one successful login, so it passes despite violating the single-use recovery-code contract. Consume codes in the fixture and extend the test to verify replay rejection, advancement, and regeneration after exhaustion.
